brief: Ihāia Te Ahu of Ngā Puhi was one of the earliest of the Māori clergy. He joined Thomas Chapman of the Church Missionary Society in the Bay of Islands as a small boy, and later went with Chapman to Rotorua and then to Maketū in the Bay of Plenty. On Chapman’s retirement in 1861 Ihāia was ordained, serving first in Maketū and then in 1882 becoming the first vicar of the Ōhinemutu pastorate. Ihāia’s godly, patient ministry in complex and challenging circumstances eventually became very influential. He died in 1895.
